newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RUGBY UNION-CAMPESE BOWS OUT OF INTERNATIONAL SCENE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CAMPESE BOWS OUT OF INTERNATIONAL SCENE.

text.p: Australia winger David Campese, the leading try scorer in world rugby union, made a losing farewell to the international game at the World Cup Sevens on Sunday.
Campese, who scored 64 tries in 101 appearances for Australia at 15-a-side, played in the quarter-final match with New Zealand which the sevens' Wallabies lost 38-12.

Although he has come to the end of his international career, Campese, 34, will continue to play top rugby and after the tournament will fly to South Africa for New South Wales' Super 12 match against Natal on March 29.
Campese, a regular at the annual Hong Kong Sevens in his heyday, said that he hoped the tournament would survive professionalism and the handover of Hong Kong to Chinese rule on July 1 this year.
"I hope the sevens survives - there's too much politics in sport," he said.
He added that among all his great moments in the game, one in particular remained fresh in his memory.
"The moment that stands out is when I pulled on the Australian jersey for the first time in 1982 when we played New Zealand - I was a young kid who knew nothing about rugby," he said.
